notes: Track 1 TIER 2 -- discriminative tool-calling battery. Tier 1 (toolcall_cases.json)
saturated at 90/90, so it is a floor and cannot rank models. These cases add pressure
along axes Tier 1 never exercised: several independent calls in one turn, nested and
union-typed argument schemas, the correct tool rotated OUT of the last position, tool
selection that turns on a single prompt constraint, and argument coercion from words.
Run with: toolcall_battery.py <spec> <rundir> --cases toolcall_cases_tier2.json
The driver copies this file into the run dir, so grading is self-contained and an edit
here can never re-grade a committed run. Same standing rules as Tier 1: --disable-tools
at launch, enable_tools:false per request, temperature 0 (greedy pass/fail), raw healing
rung by default -- apply the ladder only where a model fails at raw.
GRADER FORMS this battery relies on (see grade_sweep.grade_toolcall):
expect.calls   -- list of {name, args_match}; each must match a DISTINCT actual call,
order-insensitive. Used by tc_parallel.
args_match [ ] -- a pattern VALUE may be a list; all patterns must match the one arg.
Used to assert several substrings inside a nested object/array arg.
PROMPT-TOKEN CEILINGS are per case (expect.max_prompt_tokens), ~2x the clean baseline,
so a distractor case's five schemas are not flagged as injection while a real server-side
tools-back-on event (2000-16000 tokens) still trips the flag.
UNVALIDATED-AGAINST-LIVE-SERVER: authored offline (both inference boxes were occupied).
The JSON round-trips through the grader's synthetic fixtures in test_grade_toolcall.py,
but the prompt wordings have not yet been confirmed to elicit the intended calls from a
real model. First live run should sanity-check that at least one strong model passes each
case before the scores are read as a ranking.

tc_parallel.intent: Three independent calls in ONE turn. Catches models that can only emit a single tool_call per assistant message, or that serialise what should be parallel. Graded order-insensitively so call ordering is not penalised.
tc_parallel.prompt: Get the current temperature in Denver, Boston, and Seattle. Call the weather tool once for each city in this turn; do not guess and do not wait between calls.

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the current weather for a city.

tc_nested.intent: One call whose arguments are a nested object plus an array of objects. Catches models that flatten structure or drop line-items. args_match uses list-of-patterns to assert both SKUs and the customer inside the serialised argument.
tc_nested.prompt: Place an order for customer Ada Lovelace (tier: gold): 2 units of SKU AX-19 and 5 units of SKU BX-7, with rush shipping. Use the order tool.

function.name: create_order
function.description: Create a customer order with one or more line items.

tc_union.intent: A union-typed argument (anyOf: a preset enum OR a structured object). The prompt pins an exact timestamp, which only the object branch can express, so a model that collapses the union to the enum fails. Discriminates schema-following depth.
tc_union.prompt: Schedule a reminder for exactly 2026-09-01 at 14:30 (not a vague time of day). Use the reminder tool.

function.name: set_reminder
function.description: Set a reminder at either a preset time of day or an exact datetime.

when.description: Either a preset slot or an exact datetime object.

tc_distractor_p1.intent: tc_distractor with the correct tool (convert_currency) moved to POSITION 1 of 5. Paired with tc_distractor (pos 5) and tc_distractor_p3 (pos 3), it isolates positional bias in tool selection -- a model that pattern-matches the first offered tool passes here but should also pass tc_distractor.
tc_distractor_p1.prompt: How much is 250 US dollars in euros right now? Use the available tools.

function.name: convert_currency
function.description: Convert an amount from one currency to another at the live rate.

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the current weather for a city.

function.name: send_email
function.description: Send an email to a recipient.

function.name: search_flights
function.description: Search for flights between two airports.

tc_distractor_p3.intent: tc_distractor with the correct tool (convert_currency) at POSITION 3 of 5 (the middle). Third leg of the positional-bias triple with tc_distractor (pos 5) and tc_distractor_p1 (pos 1).
tc_distractor_p3.prompt: How much is 250 US dollars in euros right now? Use the available tools.

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the current weather for a city.

function.name: send_email
function.description: Send an email to a recipient.

function.name: convert_currency
function.description: Convert an amount from one currency to another at the live rate.

function.name: search_flights
function.description: Search for flights between two airports.

tc_ambiguous.intent: Two tools both plausibly about flights; a single prompt detail (a specific flight number, not a route) selects get_flight_status over search_flights. Catches surface pattern-matching on the word 'flight'.
tc_ambiguous.prompt: Is flight UA 448 on time today? Use the available tools.

function.name: search_flights
function.description: Search for available flights between two airports on a date.

function.name: get_flight_status
function.description: Get the current status (on time, delayed, cancelled) of a specific flight by its number.

tc_coercion.intent: The amount is given in words ('fifteen hundred'), but the schema types it as a number. The model must coerce words -> 1500 rather than pass a string or refuse. Catches literal argument copying.
tc_coercion.prompt: Convert fifteen hundred US dollars into euros using the available tool.

function.name: convert_currency
function.description: Convert an amount from one currency to another at the live rate.

amount.description: Amount to convert, as a number
